newsitem.title: USA: US Plains fed cattle trade thin at $64 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: US Plains fed cattle trade thin at $64 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle trade near midday on Thursday was extremely slow at $64.00 per cwt, unchanged from this week's sales, but up $2.00 from last week's top price, feedlot sources said.

About 100 heifers that will likely grade select and choice sold in Kansas, which brought the weekly figure to 78,000 head, they said. An estimated 900 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area, with most of the showlist near sold out, the sources said. The week-to-date movement for the Panhandle was pegged near 90,000 head.
Further bids at $64.00 in the Panhandle area and Kansas were passed by owners pricing cattle at $65.00, feedlot sources said.
This week's gain in fed cattle prices was attributed to strength in the Chicago Mercantile Exchange live cattle futures and firm boxed beef cut-out values, market sources said.
Support also was attributed to ideas that some packers were short bought and needed to augment live inventories to meet demand for previously booked beef orders, they said.
